paragraphs: Friend, here's what stands out to me in this passage. The LORD handed the Levites their work with nothing left fuzzy. Three clans got three different loads: the holy objects, the curtains, the frames and posts. Nobody was standing around asking, "So what do I do?" because each one was assigned his work and burden (Numbers 4:49).

It also teaches that God is holy, and He's serious about it. The Kohathites were told not to touch the holy objects, or they would die (Numbers 4:15), and not to go in and look, even for a moment (Numbers 4:20). But look at WHY He gave the order. It was so they would "live and not die when they come near the most holy things" (Numbers 4:19), and I think that's a God who sets a boundary because He wants His people to live.

So, baker, what do you take from it? Work that God gives is never too small, because every load in that camp was assigned by the LORD, and every Levite man from thirty to fifty was counted (Numbers 4:46-49). Carrying curtains and tent pegs didn't look like much, but it was assigned by the LORD, and that is what made it matter. I know what it feels like to sit in the dark with nothing to do, so trust me: when God hands you work in His service, it is a gift.
